messages.reasoning_content: kolibri_sizes.h owns the runtime allocations: the persistent KV groups (full layers growing with max_len, sliding layers in a fixed ring), the decode scratch, and the planner that adds them up per device. It includes model/kolibri1.h and the pipeline plan, but not the loader layout - so where do the weight bytes come from? It mentions that the plan adds weight bytes; I need the layout header to see the per-layer weight formula.

00011| // Per layer (model::Kolibri1Desc's shapes; derived, the loader asserts them):
00012| //
00013| //   qkv, oproj   int4 arm: GPTQ layout 0 (words [K/8][N] + f16 scales [K/64][N]) -
00014| //                  q||k||v 2560 x 7168 (9,175,040 + 573,440 B), o_proj 6144 x 2560
00015| //                  (7,864,320 + 491,520 B): 18,104,320 B
00016| //                bf16 arm: gemv_bf16's tiles, 36,700,160 + 31,457,280 = 68,157,440 B
00017| //   router       bf16 tiled {hidden, router_n 512}, rows 384..511 zero: 2,621,440 B
00018| //   bias         fp32 [router_n]: expert_bias widened, 0 past the experts: 2,048 B
00019| //   norms        fp32 [4 x hidden + 2 x head_dim] (Kolibri1Desc::norm_off_*): 41,984 B
00020| //   gate_up      int4 layout-1 blocks [experts][hidden x 2I] (gate||up interleave16):
00021| //                  384 x 1,392,640 = 534,773,760 B
00022| //   down         int4 layout-1 blocks [experts][I x hidden]: 384 x 696,320 = 267,386,880 B
00023| //   shared       bf16 tiled {hidden, 2I} (gate||up interleave16) 5,242,880 B and
00024| //                  {I, hidden} 2,621,440 B: 7,864,320 B
00025| //   total        830,794,752 B (int4 attention), 880,847,872 B (bf16 attention)
00026| //
00027| // Top level: embed bf16 [vocab][hidden] 655,360,000 B (device 0, gathered); lm_head bf16 tiled
00028| // 655,360,000 B or int8 + fp32 row scales 328,192,000 B, and the final norm fp32 [hidden]
00029| // (the last device); the RoPE table fp32 [max_len][2][64] on every device holding a sliding
00030| // layer (Kolibri1Desc::rope_table_bytes - the one term that scales with max_len).
00031| // The real model, int4 attention, int8 head, split 25: device 0 21,425,228,800 B, device 1
00032| // 21,098,071,040 B (derived; kolibri1_repack_test pins it).
00033| namespace loader {
00034| 
00035| inline constexpr uint32_t kKolTileU32 = 136;   // layout 1: 128 nibble + 8 scale u32 per tile
00036| 
00037| inline constexpr size_t kol_layout1_bytes(uint32_t K, uint32_t N) {
00038|   return size_t(N / 16) * (K / 64) * kKolTileU32 * 4;
00039| }
00040| inline constexpr size_t kol_layout0_bytes(uint32_t K, uint32_t N) {
00041|   return size_t(K / 8) * N * 4 + size_t(K / 64) * N * 2;
00042| }
00043| 
00044| struct KolLayerBytes {
00045|   size_t qkv = 0, oproj = 0, router = 0, bias = 0, norms = 0, gate_up = 0, down = 0, shared_gate_up = 0,
00046|          shared_down = 0;
00047|   size_t total() const { return qkv + oproj + router + bias + norms + gate_up + down + shared_gate_up + shared_down; }
00048|   size_t experts() const { return gate_up + down; }
00049|   size_t attention() const { return qkv + oproj; }
00050| };
00051| 
00052| inline size_t kol_linear_bytes(const model::Kolibri1Desc& d, model::KolLinearId id) {
00053|   const model::GemvShape s = d.linear(id).shape;
00054|   return d.attn == model::KolAttnForm::Int4 ? kol_layout0_bytes(s.K, s.N) : size_t(s.K) * s.N * 2;
00055| }
00056| 
00057| inline KolLayerBytes kol_layer_bytes(const model::Kolibri1Desc& d) {
00058|   KolLayerBytes b;
00059|   b.qkv = kol_linear_bytes(d, model::KolLinearId::Qkv);
00060|   b.oproj = kol_linear_bytes(d, model::KolLinearId::OProj);
00061|   b.router = size_t(d.router_n()) * d.hidden * 2;
00062|   b.bias = size_t(d.router_n()) * 4;
00063|   b.norms = size_t(d.norm_floats()) * 4;
00064|   b.gate_up = kol_layout1_bytes(d.hidden, 2 * d.moe_inter) * d.experts;
00065|   b.down = kol_layout1_bytes(d.moe_inter, d.hidden) * d.experts;
00066|   b.shared_gate_up = size_t(d.hidden) * 2 * d.shared_inter * 2;
00067|   b.shared_down = size_t(d.shared_inter) * d.hidden * 2;
00068|   return b;
00069| }
00070| // One expert's block in `gate_up` / `down` (block e at e x this).
00071| inline size_t kol_gate_up_block_bytes(const model::Kolibri1Desc& d) {
00072|   return kol_layout1_bytes(d.hidden, 2 * d.moe_inter);
00073| }
00074| inline size_t kol_down_block_bytes(const model::Kolibri1Desc& d) { return kol_layout1_bytes(d.moe_inter, d.hidden); }
00075| 
00076| inline size_t kol_embed_bytes(const model::Kolibri1Desc& d) { return size_t(d.vocab) * d.hidden * 2; }
00077| inline size_t kol_lm_head_bytes(const model::Kolibri1Desc& d, bool int8) {
00078|   return int8 ? size_t(d.vocab) * d.hidden + size_t(d.vocab) * 4 : size_t(d.vocab) * d.hidden * 2;
00079| }
00080| inline size_t kol_final_norm_bytes(const model::Kolibri1Desc& d) { return size_t(d.hidden) * 4; }
00081| 
00082| // A device's weights under a placement (the RoPE table excluded): its layers, the embedding on
00083| // device 0, the final norm and lm_head on the last device.
00084| inline size_t kol_device_weight_bytes(const model::Kolibri1Desc& d, const model::KolPlacement& p,
00085|                                       uint32_t dev, bool int8_head) {
00086|   size_t b = size_t(p.count(dev)) * kol_layer_bytes(d).total();

00088|   if (dev + 1 == p.devices) b += kol_final_norm_bytes(d) + kol_lm_head_bytes(d, int8_head);
00089|   return b;
00090| }
00091| // Whether device `dev` holds a sliding layer (and so a RoPE table).
00092| inline bool kol_device_has_sliding(const model::Kolibri1Desc& d, const model::KolPlacement& p, uint32_t dev) {
00093|   for (uint32_t l = p.first(dev); l < p.end(dev); ++l)
00094|     if (d.is_sliding(l)) return true;
00095|   return false;
00096| }
00097| 
00098| // What ONE decode token reads of a layer (derived): attention, router, bias, norms, top_k
00099| // expert blocks and the shared expert.
00100| inline size_t kol_layer_read_per_token(const model::Kolibri1Desc& d) {
00101|   const KolLayerBytes b = kol_layer_bytes(d);
00102|   return b.qkv + b.oproj + b.router + b.bias + b.norms +
00103|          size_t(d.top_k) * (kol_gate_up_block_bytes(d) + kol_down_block_bytes(d)) + b.shared_gate_up +
00104|          b.shared_down;
00105| }

messages.reasoning_content: kolibri1_layout.h is header-only on purpose: its comment says the planner and the loader share it, so the weight bytes have one home. But kolibri_sizes.h computes full_kv_bytes_per_pos and ring bytes itself - those are runtime buffers, not weights, so that is not a duplicate. The question is whether kolibri_sizes.cc re-derives any weight number instead of calling kol_layer_bytes. Grep for the layout helpers and for a hand-written 136 or layout-1 formula outside the layout header.

Good: both the loader and the planner call loader::kol_layer_bytes, and the only tile constant is in the layout header. The KV formulas live only in kolibri_sizes.h. One more place to check: the RoPE table, which the layout comment says scales with max_len and is counted via Kolibri1Desc::rope_table_bytes - make sure kolibri_sizes.cc does not count it a second time in the persistent group.
